standard_prerequisites.name: Homotopy classes of maps between complexes of modules over a quotient coincide over the ring and over the quotient when the ring map is an epimorphism
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Algebra, Lemma \ref{algebra-lemma-epimorphism-modules}, cited at proof lines 13949-13952
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the identification that transfers the K-injectivity property.

core_obligations: Identify the two homotopy module sets over the ring and over the quotient (proof lines 13948-13952).
Conclude that K-injectivity over the ring implies K-injectivity over the quotient (proof lines 13952-13953).
proof_roadmap: The identification of homotopy classes (proof lines 13948-13952).
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that a complex of modules over a ring which is an epimorphic quotient is K-injective as a complex over that quotient as soon as it is K-injective as a complex over the ring. The proof is short: over an epimorphism, the set of homotopy classes of maps from a complex of quotient modules to the given complex is the same whether computed over the ring or over the quotient, so the defining lifting property of K-injectivity transfers.
